original_question: Let C be a simple planar closed curve of length L, and let D be the planar domain bounded by C. For every H in the interval [0, L/(2|D|)], does there exist a compact surface of constant mean curvature H bounded by C? In particular, what happens when C is convex or when C is an ellipse?

Your added convex/ellipse clause drifts into nearby but distinct follow-up items, especially Proposition 1.2 / Problem 3.2 (the endpoint H = L/(2|D|)) and Theorem 1.3 / Problem 3.6 (the convex-cylinder graph question).

It also correctly senses that convexity and ellipses are discussed nearby in the paper, though those belong to adjacent, more specialized questions rather than to the exact main formulation.
missing_details: The ambient space should be stated explicitly: the surfaces live in Euclidean three-space R^3.
C should be specified as a simple closed planar (Jordan) curve lying in a plane P ⊂ R^3, and D is the bounded planar domain in P enclosed by C.

The paper's notion is an H-surface with boundary C, i.e. a compact connected immersed surface Σ ⊂ R^3 of constant mean curvature H whose boundary is mapped diffeomorphically onto C; your draft does not say whether immersion, embeddedness, or disk topology is assumed.
The official core question does not assume convexity, embeddedness, or that Σ is a disk.
The endpoint H = L/(2|D|) is separated out in nearby discussion: Proposition 1.2 / Problem 3.2 isolate this extremal case and identify the boundary-plane orthogonality phenomenon there.

The convex case is not part of the exact Conjecture 1.1 / Problem 3.1 formulation; it belongs to the separate nearby question asking, under the extra hypothesis Σ ⊂ D × R, whether Σ must be a graph over D.
The ellipse case is likewise not the official main formulation; it is only a special case of those neighboring convex/endpoint questions.
Your draft does not distinguish the general existence problem for all H in the interval from the special extremal case H = L/(2|D|), which the paper treats separately.
The sign convention is implicitly normalized by asking for H in [0, L/(2|D|)] rather than both signs; your draft does not explain that this is the paper's chosen scope.
refined_question: Let C ⊂ P ⊂ R^3 be a simple closed planar curve of length L, and let D ⊂ P be the bounded domain enclosed by C. Is it true that for every H ∈ [0, L/(2|D|)] there exists a compact connected immersed surface Σ ⊂ R^3 of constant mean curvature H whose boundary is C (equivalently, the boundary map is a diffeomorphism from ∂Σ onto C)?
justification: The draft is closest to the paper's planar-boundary existence conjecture, not to the neighboring convex-graph or ellipse-special-case questions. In the paper's Introduction, Conjecture 1.1 asks for existence of a compact H-surface spanning a simple closed planar curve for every H up to the Heinz bound; Section 3 restates this as Problem 3.1. The nearby Introduction items Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3, together with Section 3 Problems 3.2 and 3.6, explain why your extra convex/ellipse language is nearby but not part of the exact official formulation: the endpoint H = L/(2|D|) is singled out because it forces orthogonality to the boundary plane, while the convex case in the paper carries the extra containment hypothesis Σ ⊂ D × R and asks whether Σ is a graph over D. So the paper-faithful refinement is to state only the full general planar-boundary existence question, explicitly in R^3 and without importing the extra convex/ellipse hypotheses into the main problem.
